metadata.title: OmO
metadata.description: Your tool for real work. But it's an agent. OmO turns your tokens into results that matter.

hero.title: Your tool for real work.
hero.subcopy:
Turn your tokens into results that matter.
Research across ten thousand sources. A deck people actually get.
Company work, experiments, backends, frontends, code.
Whatever you need done.

secret.lead: We'd rather you never had to read what's below.
secret.body:
Focus on your work.
OmO takes care of the tech.
The more you use it, the better it fits you.
secret.reveal: Still curious? This is for you.

ultrawork.title: ultrawork
ultrawork.body: Skip the study. If a task feels hard, add the word ultrawork to your prompt. The agent decides how to attack it and drives to the best result on its own.
ultrawork.promptPrefix: make the quarterly report actually readable
ultrawork.step1: reads the whole codebase before touching a line
ultrawork.step2: plans, then proves each step before moving on
ultrawork.step3: verifies the result on the real surface, then stops

multiModel.title: Mix models without thinking about it.
multiModel.body: Use the frontier models you love together with the cheap ones. Just sign in. Every model ships with a system prompt tuned for it, so you never pick the wrong one.
multiModel.caption: Tuned profiles shipped with OmO

ulw.title: Hundreds of agents working for you. One keyword.
ulw.body: Type mass ulw and the whole job becomes a graph of agents: deep research over thousands of sources, a full machine-learning pipeline, a migration nobody wants to do. Each part runs on the model that fits it, in parallel, and gets checked before anything is called done.

kibitzer.title: Kibitzer. Your agent doesn't forget you, or your work.
kibitzer.body: A small, cheap model sits beside the expensive main agent, reads what you've done before, and nudges the main agent before it repeats a mistake. The expensive model stays sharp; you stop re-explaining yourself.
kibitzer.scene: A small, cheap Kibitzer loops through watching and reading memory beside the expensive main agent's independent loop, inserting a reminder to run the migration test before shipping.
kibitzer.memoryNote: Previous migration: production broke when the test was skipped.
kibitzer.testFirst: Verify · run the migration test first
kibitzer.reason: Last time this broke production. Run the migration test first.

skills.title: High-quality skills. Only the ones you need.
skills.body: Your model is smart, but it still doesn't know a lot about solving real-world problems. OmO ships the missing knowledge as skills and loads only what the task needs.

crafted.title: And everything else you'll touch is crafted.
crafted.body: You won't see most of this. That's the point.
crafted.docs: Read the details in the docs
crafted.item1Desc: Independent tool calls run together in one small program instead of one slow round trip each.
crafted.item2Desc: Dozens of read, search and lookup calls collapse into a single step. Fewer turns, less waiting, fewer tokens.
crafted.item3Desc: Malformed arguments are repaired before they execute, so a typo never becomes a wasted turn.
crafted.item4Desc: A lead agent runs a team of specialists in parallel when a job is big enough to split.
crafted.item5Desc: Waiting on a build, a deploy or a file is a subscription. The agent keeps working and wakes when it lands.
crafted.item6Desc: Long work is checkpointed with evidence, so a session restart resumes where it stopped.
crafted.item7Desc: Config, skills and prompts reload live. No restarts to try a change.

platforms.body: Talk to your agent where you already are. It messages as you, not as a bot, on every platform you use.
platforms.footnote: Coming soon. Messaging platforms are being wired in one by one.

hero.title: Ultrawork Manifesto
hero.subtitle:
We build today's tools, and tomorrow's,
so you can keep your head in your work.

yourWork.title: Your work
yourWork.p1:
You boot up your laptop. You open Slack.
Every day we sit at a keyboard and a mouse and do the same work as everyone else.
Except it isn't the same.
Every day, we mix in a little of our own wisdom and experience.
yourWork.p2:
Nobody else has your wisdom and experience.
That's what makes your work worth something.
yourWork.p3:
Your work matters.
Not because you dug up piles of material, set up an experiment, and wrote the code.
Because your wisdom and experience went into it.
The rest was just your hands moving.

ourTool.title: The tool we build
ourTool.p1: Agents today can act on your behalf.
ourTool.p2:
They read dozens of times more than you ever could,
throw all of human knowledge at the question of how to build it,
and they work 24 hours a day.
ourTool.p3:
So it ought to be simple.
You put in quality tokens and compute,
and great work comes out.
ourTool.p4: That's what today's tool has to be.
ourTool.p5:
Which harness, which model's quirks, which skills...
none of that should be your problem.
ourTool.p6: When your wisdom meets quality tokens, it should compile straight into good work.
ourTool.p7:
That's the tool we're building.
It takes your quality tokens and turns them into great work.

ourThinking.title: What we think
ourThinking.p1:
Agents today can act on your behalf,
but they don't have your wisdom or your experience.
ourThinking.p2:
Give them everything you know, and then some.
What you picked up by living as a human
still won't come out of the few characters an agent uses to make sense of the world.
ourThinking.p3Link: We already live in a world where AI cracks a Millennium Prize problem,
ourThinking.p3Rest: and even that proof grew from one seed, a single line of human wisdom.
ourThinking.p4:
We value your wisdom and experience.
And everyone else's, just as much.
ourThinking.p5:
Our tool takes someone's wisdom and experience, and how they got there,
and hands it to you, still alive.
ourThinking.p6:
Our own thinking reaches you as living wisdom.
Under the name of an agent. Under the name of a tool.
ourThinking.p7:
Your thinking can reach someone else the same way.
Then everyone gets to spend their time on the problems that actually matter to them,
and solve those.
We think we can build that world.

tomorrow.title: Tomorrow's tool
tomorrow.p1:
When everyone shares what they know,
when people think up the countless problems that matter to them and toss them out,
and computers just come back with the answers,
tomorrow.p2:
we'll show up again, with tomorrow's tool,
so you can focus one more time.

manifesto.legacyNote: Back on <date>January 19, 2026</date> we said an agent that makes you read its code is a badly built tool. <link>Read the old version</link>

manifestoLegacy.autonomousCar: Imagine an autonomous car that makes you grab the wheel every 30 seconds. Would you call that "autonomous"? No. You'd call it driver assist. Barely better than cruise control.
manifestoLegacy.micromanagement: We've accepted a version of "AI coding" where a chatbot writes 20 lines, then waits for you to fix them. Nobody would call that automation. It's micromanagement.

painPoints.reviewing: Reviewing every single line for hallucinations

manifestoLegacy.notCollaboration: That's not "human-AI collaboration." That's the AI failing to do its job.
manifestoLegacy.premise: {linkText} is built on the premise that the human should be the architect, not the spell-checker.

indistinguishable.title: Indistinguishable Code
indistinguishable.subtitle: Agent-written code should be indistinguishable from code written by a senior engineer.

items.patterns: Follows existing codebase patterns and architecture
items.errorHandling: Handles errors and edge cases without being asked
items.tests: Writes tests that actually test behavior, not just coverage
items.noSlop: No AI slop, meaning no over-engineering and no abstractions nobody asked for
items.comments: Comments only when they add value, never to restate the obvious

indistinguishable.quote: "If you can tell whether a commit was made by a human or an agent, the agent has failed."

tokenCost.title: Token Cost vs. Productivity
tokenCost.description: We don't care about token usage. We care about output. If spending $5 on tokens saves an hour of engineering time, that's a 20x ROI.
tokenCost.selfVerification: Verifies its own work before calling it done
tokenCost.optimizeDescription: We optimize for efficiency where it counts. Not by crippling the model, but by:
tokenCost.cheaperModels: Using cheaper models for routine tasks
tokenCost.avoidingRedundant: Not exploring the same ground twice
tokenCost.intelligentCaching: Caching what it learned across sessions

cognitiveLoad.title: Minimize Human Cognitive Load
cognitiveLoad.subtitle: The human should only need to say what they want. Everything else is the agent's job.

steps.breakdown: Breaks the task into atomic steps

plannerExecutor.title: Planner + Executor
plannerExecutor.subtitle: When you want strategic control.
plannerExecutor.plannerDescription: Interviews you and researches the codebase, then writes a detailed work plan.
plannerExecutor.executorDescription: Executes the approved plan in the same session, delegating by category and tracking progress wave by wave.
plannerExecutor.footer: You architect. Agents execute. Nothing happens out of sight.

predictable.title: Predictable
predictable.description: Same inputs, same output. No surprises and no creative liberties you didn't ask for.

continuous.title: Continuous
continuous.description: Work survives a crashed session or a week away, because the agent keeps the state and you don't have to.

delegatable.title: Delegatable
delegatable.description: Hand it a task with clear acceptance criteria, the way you'd hand one to a capable teammate. It corrects itself when something goes wrong and escalates only when it has to.

planner.purpose: Draw out what you actually want before anything gets built

planConsultant.purpose: Catch ambiguities before they become bugs

planReviewer.purpose: Verify the plan is complete before execution

orchestrator.purpose: Coordinate the work so you don't have to micromanage it

categorySystem.purpose: Route each task to the right model so you never have to pick one

backgroundAgents.purpose: Research in parallel without blocking you

wisdomAccumulation.purpose: Learn from work, don't repeat mistakes

future.title: The Future We're Building

items.focus: Developers think about what to build, not how to get an AI to build it
items.quality: Code quality that doesn't depend on who wrote it
items.complexity: Complex projects as easy as simple ones

future.quote1: "The agent should be invisible. Like electricity, like running water."
future.quote2: "You flip the switch. The light turns on. You don't think about the power grid."

archive.note: Written when not reading the code was still called crazy, and everyone sat in front of the agent.
